The upper and lower bounds use different outputs of the transfer: squared overlap bounds the covariance norm from above, while the top projection bounds it from below.

outputs.exact_statement: For every positive deterministic sequence $M_n\to\infty$, with probability tending to one both $\|\Sigma\|$ and $\mathcal R_{\rm lin}(\mu_W)$ belong to $$\left[\frac{n^{2/3}}{M_n},\ M_n n^{2/3}\right].$$

Each $P_i$ is an orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mu)$. The unscaled Dirichlet form is $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D_\mu(f)
 &=-\langle f,\mathcal Lf\rangle_\mu
   =\sum_i\mu[(f-P_if)^2]  \label{eq:heatbath-form}\\
 &=\sum_i\inf_{h_i:\{-1,1\}^{n-1}\to\mathbb R}
       \mu[(f-h_i(x_{-i}))^2].\nonumber
\end{aligned}$$ The discrete form is $\langle f,(\mathrm{Id}-P)f\rangle_\mu=\mathcal D_\mu(f)/n$, and $P$ has spectrum in $[0,1]$. For a linear function, $$\label{eq:linear-form}
 \mathcal D_\mu(a^Tx)=\sum_i a_i^2\alpha_i,
 \qquad
 \alpha_i=\mu[\mathop{\mathrm{sech}}^2 g_i],\quad
 g_i(x)=\sum_{j\ne i}W_{ij}x_j.$$

There is a universal constant $C_0$ such that, with $$\Phi_n(x)=C_0n^{-1/2}A_n(x+s_0)^{1/4}
             \sqrt{1+\log(1+x/s_0)},\qquad x\ge0,$$ the matrix $H=T-D$ satisfies, simultaneously for every unit vector $u\in\mathbb R^n$, $$|u^THu|\le\Phi_n(u^TEu)
 \label{eq:form-bound}$$ on an event $\mathcal F_n$ with $\mathbb P(\mathcal F_n^c)\le C\exp(-cL_n^{1/4})$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Moreover, $$\sup_{x\ge0}|\Phi_n'(x)|\le C\eta_n,
 \qquad \Phi_n(0)\le C\eta_ns_0.
 \label{eq:phi-smallness}$$

Let $e_1\le\cdots\le e_n$ be the eigenvalues of $E=2I-D$, and set $$R_D(s)=\frac1n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}(s+E)^{-1},\qquad
 T_D(s)=\frac1n\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}(s+E)^{-2}=-R_D'(s).$$ For every fixed $M<\infty$ and all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly for $s_0\le s\le M$, $$T_D(s)\le C_Ms^{-1/2},\qquad
 0\le R(s)-R_D(s)\le\frac{C_M}{ns}.
 \label{eq:deterministic-traces}$$ Moreover, $$N(t):=\#\{i:e_i\le t\}\le Cnt^{3/2}
 \qquad(t\ge s_0).
 \label{eq:deterministic-counting}$$

There is a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for every $n\ge3$ and every $k_1,\ldots,k_n>0$ with $\sum_i k_i=n$, the density $p$ of $\sum_i k_iG_i^2$, for independent standard Gaussians $G_i$, satisfies $$\label{eq:mean-density}
 p(n)\ge c\left(\sum_i k_i^2\right)^{-1/2}.$$

With the preceding notation, $$\label{eq:critical-spherical-parameters}
 \lambda_1<z_1<2+s_0,\qquad
 \left(\sum_i k_i^2\right)^{1/2}\le Cn\sqrt{s_0},
 \qquad
 k_j\ge c/s_0\quad(1\le j\le3).$$ Moreover, $$p(n)\ge \frac{c}{n\sqrt{s_0}},
 \qquad
 \sup_{r\in\mathbb R}p_{-i}(r)\le Cs_0
 \quad(1\le i\le n).$$

The probability $\sigma_\Lambda$ has mean zero and diagonal covariance in the eigenbasis of $\Lambda$. For every coordinate, $$\label{eq:spherical-coordinate-moment}
 \int u_i^2\,\sigma_\Lambda(du)
 \le \frac{Cs_0 k_i}{p(n)}.$$ Consequently, for independent $U,V$ with law $\sigma_\Lambda$, $$\label{eq:spherical-overlap}
 \mathbb E\left(\frac{U^TV}{n}\right)^2
 \le
 \frac{Cs_0^2}{n^2p(n)^2}\sum_i k_i^2
 \le Cn^{-2/3}L_n^4.$$

There is a universal constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, uniformly for spectra in $\mathcal G_n$ and $q_0\le q\le1$, $$B(1+q)+B(1-q)-2B(1)
 \le \frac{q^2}{2}-cq^3.
 \label{eq:cubic-deficit}$$ One may take $c=1/24$.

For spectra in $\mathcal G_n$, $$\mathbb E_O I=S(1),
 \qquad
 \sup_{\Lambda\in\mathcal G_n}
 \mathbb E_O\!\left[\left(\frac{I}{S(1)}-1\right)^2\right]\longrightarrow0.$$ In particular, under the GOE law, $I/S(1)\to1$ in probability.

Let $W$ be the augmented GOE matrix and let $v$ be a unit top eigenvector. For every positive deterministic sequence $b_n\to0$, $$\mu\{x:|v^Tx|\le b_n n^{1/3}\}
 \longrightarrow0
 \quad\text{in probability}.
 \label{eq:static-small-ball}$$ The probability here includes the auxiliary diagonal used to define $v$; the Gibbs measure itself does not depend on that diagonal.

Let $Q_n=\mathbb E_{\mu^{\otimes2}}q(x,y)^2$. Then $n^{2/3}Q_n$ is bounded in probability. Equivalently, for every positive deterministic sequence $T_n\to\infty$, $$\mathbb P\{n^{2/3}Q_n>T_n\}\longrightarrow0.
 \label{eq:orientation-overlap-tail}$$ This assertion concerns the original off-diagonal SK disorder.

Fix the disorder and a function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Let $(X_t)_{t\ge0}$ be the continuous-time heat-bath chain with generator $\mathcal L$, and let $(Y_k)_{k\ge0}$ be the discrete-time chain with transition operator $P$, each started from $\mu$. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_\mu\bigl[(f(X_t)-f(X_0))^2\bigr]
 &\le 2t\,\mathcal D_\mu(f), \qquad t\ge0,\label{eq:stationary-increments-ct}\\
 \mathbb E_\mu\bigl[(f(Y_k)-f(Y_0))^2\bigr]
 &\le \frac{2k}{n}\,\mathcal D_\mu(f),
 \qquad k\in\{0,1,2,\ldots\}.\label{eq:stationary-increments-dt}
\end{aligned}$$ Here the expectations average only over the initial configuration and the trajectory. In particular, if $g(x)=v^Tx$ and $\|v\|=1$, the two right-hand sides are at most $2t$ and $2k/n$, respectively.

Fix $0<\beta<1$. Let $J$ be a symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and independent entries $J_{ij}\sim N(0,\beta^2/n)$ for $i<j$, and let $$\nu_J(x)=Z_J^{-1}\exp\bigl(\tfrac12x^TJx\bigr),
 \qquad x\in\{-1,1\}^n.$$ There is a finite constant $C_\beta$, depending only on $\beta$, such that $$\mathbb P_J\!\left\{
   \mathop{\mathrm{Var}}_{\nu_J}(f)\le C_\beta\mathcal D_{\nu_J}(f)
   \text{ for every }f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R
 \right\}\longrightarrow1.$$ Here $\mathcal D_{\nu_J}$ is the unscaled sum of conditional variances. Consequently, the discrete-time heat-bath chain choosing one uniform site has spectral gap at least $1/(nC_\beta)$ with probability tending to one.

Fix any realization of the SK measure on $\Omega_n$, $n\ge2$. For every positive integer $r$, there is an irreducible, aperiodic, reversible Markov kernel with stationary law $\mu$ whose worst-state threshold-$1/4$ mixing time equals $r$.
For $n=2$ and the discrete uniform-site heat-bath kernel, the mixing time has no finite deterministic essential upper bound over the Gaussian coupling, although it is finite for every realization.

purpose: Critical slowing down in the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model

coverage.checked_domain: The seven listed rational two-spin refresh instances, including zero steps, full refresh, an exact threshold, and instances on both sides of the threshold. Arbitrary real stationary laws and arbitrary prescribed target times are outside the executed domain.
coverage.oracle_basis: Exact finite transition-matrix powers and row total variation are compared with the independently evaluated identity (1-p)^k times (1-mu_min). The uniform p=2/3 case reaches the threshold at step 1; the uniform and nonuniform p=1/2 cases cross it between steps 1 and 2.
